description:
Create a Stripe embedded-checkout link for an existing order, only when the customer asks to pay.

The link locks the order to its design for good, so never create it just
because the customer picked or finished a design.

Only for orders created in this session (`OrderNotInSessionError`
otherwise) — an order someone mentions or that `order_lookup` found
cannot be paid here, so offer to escalate rather than retrying.

Attaches each item's design to its own item once every item is covered.
Each item needs a design or artwork with a submitted page mapping.
Uses each design's latest snapshot, so the customer gets the version they
last refined. Do NOT call `order_attach_design` yourself, even on an order
with several items. Attaching is irreversible upstream, and doing it earlier
locks the order onto a draft the customer has since edited. A file uploaded
for an item after its design, before the attach, replaces that design.

Every line must carry artwork before the order can be paid
(`ArtworkRequiredError` otherwise) — either a design (attached
here, at `order_create` time, or via `order_attach_design`) or a
finished artwork file uploaded through `order_get_artwork_upload_page`. A
multi-item order is one Stripe checkout, so a multi-line cart is payable
once each line is covered. `DesignRenderFailedError` means an attached
design's print file failed to render. The design on this order cannot be
changed, so no retry here helps; the reason says how to place a new order. `NoSnapshotError` means the
session's design is not saved yet; a photo book can take a few minutes
after it resolves. Wait a little and call this again. After 5 tries
without a saved design it becomes `ArtworkStillRequiredError`.

Returns a job — poll until SUCCEEDED for the `checkout_url`. Put
`checkout_url` in your reply as a markdown hyperlink (never the raw URL),
and call `order_get` yourself to confirm payment. When the payment card is
displayed, it shows a "Pay securely" button wired to the link and polls
`order_get` itself once clicked, so just confirm the payment step is ready
and share the link again only if the customer asks for it.
name: order_create_payment_link

anyOf.description:
The Runner's response to a `@runner.job` invocation.

On the fast path (work completed within budget), `status` is SUCCEEDED
or FAILED and `result` / `error` is populated. On the slow path,
`status` is RUNNING and `job_id` is the handle the host LLM uses for
`poll()`.

On FAILED, `error` is the safe class-name code; `reason` / `detail` are
populated only when the failure carries a host-safe explanation (e.g. a
RendReal rejection's server message + body), else they stay None.

On RUNNING, `note` carries model-facing guidance: it tells the host LLM whether
a widget is already polling the job, or whether it must call `poll_job` itself.

Canonical short-circuit response shape.

`status` is always `"error"` — acts as a discriminator for LLM consumers.
`error` is a machine-readable code (e.g. `session_not_found`).
`reason` is a human-readable explanation of why the call failed.
`detail` carries structured extra context (ids, available values, etc.).

title: Create a payment link
